name: texeno
description: Texeno is an online LaTeX and Typst editor for research papers, theses, dissertations, slides and CVs, and it compiles ConTeXt too. In ChatGPT, write and edit your documents, compile them to PDF, fix errors, manage BibTeX references and work with your co-authors' comments.

interface.shortDescription: LaTeX and Typst papers to PDF
interface.longDescription:
Texeno is an online LaTeX and Typst editor for academic and technical writing: research papers, journal articles, theses and dissertations, reports, slides and CVs. It compiles ConTeXt too. Connect it to ChatGPT to work on your projects in conversation.

What you can do:
- Start a new LaTeX, Typst or ConTeXt document, blank or from a template (article, thesis, slides, CV and many more), and add chapters and files.
- Keep working on a LaTeX project you started in Overleaf or on your own computer: upload its zip on texeno.com once, then open it here.
- Write and edit: sections, math, tables, figures, TikZ, BibTeX and biblatex references, Typst markup. Changes arrive as tracked suggestions you accept or reject in Texeno, unless you ask for them to be applied directly.
- Compile to PDF, read errors and warnings with their file and line, and fix them.
- Look at your figures and the pages of your compiled PDF to check the layout, and download the PDF. For security, the download link works once and expires after an hour.
- Proofread and rewrite text, search a project, count words, browse version history, and reply to or resolve your co-authors' comments.

You sign in with your Texeno account. ChatGPT sees only the projects you can open, with the same role you have on each, and you can disconnect it at any time in Texeno under Settings, Integrations. Anyone with the file open in Texeno sees the edits arrive as they are made.

Limits: new files are text files, pictures over 4 MB are described rather than shown, and compiles follow your plan's time limit in Texeno.
defaultPrompt: Fix the errors in my paper and compile it to PDF
Start a Typst report with a title page and a bibliography
Proofread my introduction and suggest changes I can accept or reject

positive.description: Lists the signed-in person's Texeno projects.
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the demo account's projects, including "Demo thesis", each with a link that opens it in Texeno.

positive.description: Reads a file from a project and summarises it.
positive.prompt: Summarise the introduction of my Demo thesis
positive.expected_behavior: Finds "Demo thesis", reads chapters/introduction.tex and gives a short summary of it, with a link to the file in Texeno. Nothing in the project changes.

positive.description: Proposes an edit as a tracked suggestion.
positive.prompt: In my Demo thesis, make the first sentence of the introduction more concise
positive.expected_behavior: Rewrites the first sentence of chapters/introduction.tex as a tracked suggestion. In Texeno the original stays visible as a suggested change until the user accepts or rejects it.

positive.description: Compiles a project and reports the result.
positive.prompt: Compile my Demo thesis and tell me if there are any errors
positive.expected_behavior: Compiles "Demo thesis" and reports whether it built, listing any errors with their file and line, and links to the PDF in Texeno.

positive.description: Creates a new project from a template.
positive.prompt: Create a new Texeno project called Lab report for a short scientific report
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a project named "Lab report" (from a fitting template, or blank with a main.tex) and returns a link that opens it in Texeno.

positive.prompt: Create a new Typst project called Field notes
positive.expected_behavior: Creates a Typst project named "Field notes" with a main.typ and returns a link that opens it in Texeno.

positive.prompt: Make my Demo thesis compile with XeLaTeX
positive.expected_behavior: Finds "Demo thesis" and sets its compiler to XeLaTeX, keeping main.tex as its main file, then says so in one line.

negative.description: A general knowledge question with nothing to do with the user's documents.
negative.prompt: What is the capital of Australia?

negative.description: A creative writing request that doesn't involve a Texeno project.
negative.prompt: Write a short poem about the ocean

negative.description: A general LaTeX question that can be answered without opening the user's projects.
negative.prompt: What is the difference between \section and \subsection in LaTeX?

publication.release_notes: Typst and ConTeXt: start, edit and compile Typst and ConTeXt documents as well as LaTeX, read their errors with file and line, search templates by language, and change a project's compiler or main file.
